problems.description: Session deletes the existing seed index.ts wholesale (-93 lines) and replaces it with unrelated ssg scaffolding instead of extending the baseline, discarding the established single-file structure and its Express/DB layer.

Files such as index-browser.ts and resolve-targets-browser.ts appear to be vendored third-party library source committed into the repo rather than pulled in as npm dependencies; they account for most of the 3021 convention violations and bloat the 4571 added lines.

3021 convention violations (convention score 0.47): classes/interfaces not PascalCase, functions not camelCase, constants not UPPER_CASE across index.ts, index-browser.ts, and resolve-targets-browser.ts — naming style inconsistent with the rest of the codebase.
jest.config.js adds a test harness pointing at src/__tests__ but the visible diff shows no corresponding test files added in this session.

strengths: Adds test infrastructure (jest.config.js with ts-jest preset) early in the story rather than deferring it
SonarQube shows genuine maintainability gains: -14 smells, -40 cognitive complexity, -7.9% duplications, +0 bugs
Package scaffolding (package.json/package-lock.json) declares explicit typed dependencies for the new project direction
commit_reviews.summary: The session improves raw maintainability metrics but lands worse overall: it discards the existing baseline and vendors non-conforming third-party source, yielding a 0.47 convention score with 3021 naming violations.

problems.description: Measured convention score is 0.47, but all 3021 cited violations are in node_modules third-party files (index-browser.ts, resolve-targets-browser.ts are @babel/core internals) — a scan artifact, not authored code; the actual committed diff (src/templates.ts, generator.ts) is convention-clean.

AST diff reports +0 classes and only +1 function, yet the commit introduces a full TemplateEngine class with 7 methods — measurement appears to undercount class/method additions relative to the visible diff.
TemplateEngine is constructed fresh on every generateSite call and template compilation is cached per-instance, so repeated generateSite invocations re-compile disk templates each time.

strengths: Extracts rendering out of generator.ts into a dedicated, well-factored TemplateEngine module with built-in defaults, disk fallback, partials loading, and compile caching — cognitive complexity dropped 10 points (SonarQube delta) while replacing ad-hoc string interpolation
Backward-compatible API: templatesDir is an optional param and nonexistent frontmatter templates/layouts fall back to builtins, so existing call sites and tests keep working
Comprehensive test suite (207-line templates.test.ts) covering defaults, disk templates, HTML escaping, raw-content passthrough, and fallback behavior
Follows repo conventions: PascalCase class, camelCase methods, optional-param style, re-export through src/index.ts, tests under src/__tests__/ matching existing files
Correct dependency handling — handlebars moved from devDependencies to dependencies in both package.json and package-lock.json to match its new runtime use
commit_reviews.summary: Strong, well-tested refactor that introduces a proper Handlebars template engine with clean module boundaries and backward-compatible defaults; the low measured convention score (0.47) is an artifact of node_modules files being scanned, not this commit's code (flagged discrepancy).

problems.description: ws and chokidar were added to production dependencies in package-lock.json; for an SSG they serve the dev-server/live-reload path and should be devDependencies, which also forces transitive deps (anymatch, braces, fill-range, fsevents, picomatch, etc.) out of dev-only into production.

Convention score 0.47 with violations in the new index.ts, index-browser.ts, and resolve-targets-browser.ts (functions should be camelCase, classes/interfaces PascalCase, constants UPPER_CASE), so the added code does not match the repo's naming conventions.
Commit message '[story] Session 3: integration' is a session label rather than a descriptive, conventional summary of the change.
The 14 new imports across 2 new files in an integration session is a large surface to absorb in a single commit; smaller incremental commits would aid review.

strengths: SonarQube delta is uniformly positive: -14 smells, -11 cognitive complexity, -7.7% duplication, +0 bugs.
Lockfile records new dependencies with integrity hashes and includes @types/ws, showing type-aware dependency management.
Adding chokidar (file watching) and ws (websocket live-reload) is a coherent dependency set for SSG dev-server integration.
commit_reviews.summary: Code health improved measurably (smells, complexity, duplication all down, no new bugs) but convention adherence is poor (0.47) and live-reload-only deps were placed in production rather than devDependencies.

A reasonable plugin-architecture refactor that reduces smells and cognitive complexity (-46, -4 smells per SonarQube) but ships loose typing, CJS/ESM mixing, and silent error swallowing that offset the gains; convention adherence stays low at 0.47 per the mechanical score, though the listed violations reference files (index-browser.ts, resolve-targets-browser.ts) untouched by this commit, and the AST's '+0 classes' contradicts the visible `export class SSG` — discrepancies between the measurements and the diff.

problems.description: Massive naming-convention violations across index.ts, index-browser.ts, resolve-targets-browser.ts: classes and interfaces not PascalCase, functions not camelCase, constants not UPPER_CASE (3021 violations, convention score 0.47).
Cognitive complexity increased by +179 with 6 new smells, indicating overly complex branching/logic in the cross_cutting additions.

Adding parallel -browser.ts module variants (index-browser, resolve-targets-browser) alongside existing modules suggests duplicated code paths instead of a shared/parameterized implementation, corroborated by +1.8% duplication.
Regression risk: cross-cutting changes touch shared modules (index.ts) while only adding 2 functions for 683 inserted lines, bloating the surface area.

strengths: Comprehensive test coverage of generateSiteIncremental (clean build, skip-unchanged, rebuild-changed, clean flag, new pages, cache pruning, deleted-page handling)
Proper test isolation via mkdtemp setup/teardown with fs.rmSync cleanup
Commit message follows the [story] Session N convention
commit_reviews.summary: The visible test file (incremental.test.ts) is well-structured and convention-clean, but the mechanical measurements — 0.47 convention score with 3021 naming violations, +179 cognitive complexity, +1.8% duplication, and 6 smells in the truncated cross_cutting files — make this commit a net-negative, convention-adherence downgrade.

compounding_issues: The seed codebase was a Todo Express API, completely unrelated to the static-site-generator story target; session 1 discarded it wholesale (deleted index.ts), so the story built on no meaningful foundation
node_modules/ was committed to git in session 1 and never addressed — 5197 tracked files and no .gitignore was ever created across all 5 sessions, bloating every commit
Compiled dist/ artifacts were committed as build output in sessions 3 and 4, then removed in session 5 — inconsistent artifact hygiene that left churn in history

The session-4 refactor introduced a parallel plugin-based API surface (SSG class, plugin.ts, plugins/*) while retaining the original functional modules (generator.ts, server.ts, templates.ts); both coexisted in the final exports rather than consolidating into one architecture
key_decisions: Full greenfield rewrite in session 1 (parser, generator, cli, types) rather than evolving the seed
Adopting a Handlebars-based TemplateEngine with a templates/ directory of .hbs files in session 2, replacing the inline HTML string rendering from session 1
Adding an integrated dev server with live reload + server tests in session 3, wiring it into the CLI
Refactoring into a plugin-driven SSG class with plugins/markdown.ts, plugins/template.ts, plugins/devserver.ts and a ssg.config.ts in session 4
Implementing content-hash-based incremental builds (CacheManager, .ssg-cache.json manifest) with --incremental/--clean CLI flags in session 5
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality rose steadily across the 5 sessions. Session 1 established a clean foundation (parser/generator/cli with jest tests from the start), session 2 deepened it with a real template engine and 207 lines of template tests, session 3 added integration (dev server + tests), session 4 produced the most architecturally ambitious change with a plugin system and config file, and session 5 added genuinely cross-cutting engineering with cache-based incremental builds backed by the largest test suite (469 lines). The final state is a coherent, test-covered static site generator. The main blemishes are hygiene issues — committed node_modules and dist/ artifacts with no .gitignore — that persisted from early sessions, and a mild architectural split where the new plugin API coexisted with the older functional modules.
